check_service_status.description: Check whether RandomFox is up and handing out foxes, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Answering at all and answering with a fox are reported separately, because a parked domain does the first and not the second.

mock_response.message: RandomFox is up and handing out foxes (112.6 ms for /floof).

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

byte_size.description: How many bytes the site answered with.

content_type.description: The media type the site answered with, application/json when it is handing out foxes.

image_url.description: The picture the check itself was given, so a green check comes with a fox. Null when the site answered without one.

message.description: A one-line summary of the result.

online.description: True when the site answered with a fox. This is the field to branch on.

reachable.description: True when the site answered at all, whatever it said.

response_time_ms.description: How long the request took, in milliseconds.

status_code.description: The HTTP status the site answered with, or null when it could not be reached.

count_foxes.description: Find out how many foxes RandomFox has right now, and which one is the newest. The collection grows as people send more foxes in, and the number is not in the API: it is the tally the site prints on its own home page, which this step reads. Use it to pin a seeded pick, to bound a fox number a workflow makes up, or to notice when new foxes have arrived.
count_foxes.name: count_foxes

fox_count.description: How many foxes the site says it has. It goes up over time and never down.

newest.description: The newest fox. The pictures are numbered from 1 upwards, so it is the last one.

fox_number.description: The fox's number, which is how a fox is named on this site: fox 78 is the one at https://randomfox.ca/?i=78, and it stays that fox for good. Keep it to fetch the same fox again later. Null only in the rare case where the site's answer carried no number.

get_fox_of_the_day.description: Pick a fox from a seed, so the same seed always picks the same fox. Seed with the date, which is the default, and a daily post that retries, or that two people run an hour apart, shows the same fox, while tomorrow shows a different one. Seed with a channel or a customer name instead and each one gets its own fox. The pick is over however many foxes the site has, so give a fox count to pin it: the collection grows, and a bigger collection means a different fox for the same seed.

parameters.description: Optional. Any text you like. The same seed always picks the same fox, so a channel name gives each channel its own fox and a date gives a fox of the day. Leave empty for today's date in UTC.

parameters.description: Optional. How many foxes to pick from. Leave empty to use however many the site has right now, which costs one request. Wire in the count a Count the foxes step reported, or write down a number, to pin the pick: the site's collection grows, and a pick over a bigger collection is a different fox for the same seed.

get_random_foxes.description: Get a handful of foxes at random in one step, for a gallery, a digest or a set of avatars. The site draws with replacement, so three draws can be the same fox three times; by default the draws are repeated until the foxes are all different, and the step reports how many requests that took. Asking for more foxes than the site has comes back short rather than looping, with complete set to false.
get_random_foxes.name: get_random_foxes

parameters.description: Optional. How many foxes to fetch, from 1 to 20. Defaults to 3. Each fox is its own request to a small free site, so keep it modest.

parameters.description: Optional, on by default. The site draws with replacement, so three draws can be the same fox three times. On, draws are repeated until the foxes are all different, which is what a gallery wants. Off, every draw is kept as it comes, which is exactly one request per fox.

description: Put a fox in your workflow with RandomFox, the free keyless picture site at randomfox.ca: click and get a fox, 124 of them and counting. Get one at random for a stand-up opener or a channel mascot, get a handful for a gallery, download one as a file to attach to an email, or get it inline as a data URI where a link will not load. Every fox has a number, so a fox worth keeping can be fetched again exactly, and a seeded pick gives the same fox all day and a new one tomorrow.
